summary: Heidi R. M. Pauwels is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA (1983) and studied at KU Leuven, Cologne, and Vrindaban, completing a PhD at Washington (1994) under Alan Entwistle. She taught at SOAS (1994–1996) and Washington (Professor from 2002).

Heike Oberlin is an Indology scholar who studied at Kerala Kalamandalam and Tübingen, completing her PhD at Würzburg (~2001–2004) and Habilitation at Tübingen (~2005–2013). She held positions at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

Heiner Eichner was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1964–1974) under Karl Hoffmann and later served on the faculty at the University of Vienna (~1989–2010).
Heinrich August Jäschke was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and as a missionary for the Moravian Church from 1857 to 1868.

Heinrich Blochmann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leipzig under Fleischer, Paris under Hase, and Calcutta. He held posts at Fort William College, Doveton College, and Aliah University, serving as principal from 1865.
Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn from ~1839 to 1843 and served on the faculty at the University of Munich from ~1865 to 1894.

Heinrich Ewald worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Göttingen under Eichhorn, Tychsen, and the Plancks, earning a doctorate in 1823. He served as professor at Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867) and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).
Heinrich Gustav Hotho was a scholar of philosophy, history, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1822 to 1826 and held an academic post there from ~1829 until 1873.

Heinrich Hettrich was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saarland, Giessen, and Munich, later holding posts at Saarland, Munich, Zurich, Marburg, and as chair of comparative linguistics at Würzburg from 1889.

Heinrich Hübschmann was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian scholar. He studied at Jena under Schleicher, Tübingen, Munich under Martin Haug, and Leipzig. He was associate professor at Leipzig (1876) and professor of comparative linguistics at Strasbourg (1877).

Heinrich Kiepert was a geographer and historian who studied at Frederick William University Berlin under August Böckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann, earning a doctorate at Jena. He worked at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and served as professor of geography at Berlin from 1874.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Caussin de Perceval, and de Chézy. He held the chair of oriental languages at Leipzig from 1836.

Heinrich Lüders was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and taught at Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1935).

Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1884–1885) and the University of Strasbourg (~1886–1888). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1915) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).
Heinrich Rückert was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena from ~1848 to 1852 and at the University of Breslau from ~1852 to 1875.
Heinrich Schliemann was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock in ~1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Hirzel, von Orelli, and Sauppe. He taught at Kantonsschule Rämibühl (~1841–1889) and became Zurich's full professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics in 1864.
Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University (~1861–1867) under Hermann Brockhaus. He held a post teaching classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at Jena, earned a PhD at Tübingen, and completed his habilitation at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz, while also studying under Jäschke, Feer, and Max Müller. He habilitated at Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied under Scherer, Goldschmidt, Roth, Windisch, and Weber at Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Berlin. He held professorships at Greifswald (1881), Heidelberg, and Berlin (chair of Celtic languages, 1901–1910).
